reason: Not refuted as INFO, but the headline number is overstated. I re-ran scratchpad/succ_mc.py (seed 11) and the reported table reproduces: s=0.954, 150 copies, early 0.1 gives P0 0.55, port 0.85, SI 0.81, {SI,port} 0.71; s=0.956 gives 0.42 / 0.93 / 0.86. I then ran 7 stress variants as in-memory patches. The ORDER held in every one: any action beats no action; never drop #37; {SI,port} is the fragile pair (0.54 at k=0); SI is robust to timing (0.78 at 300 copies with 80% ahead, against port 0.59); SI leads on silver in all variants (with g sd 0.5, 0.25 vs 0.13; with 30% of variant teams stacking their own tweaks on the successor, 0.26 vs 0.10). The MAGNITUDE did not hold. With k=0 the bronze swing is +0.14-0.18; with k=0 and successor private noise sd 0.5 it is only +0.06-0.07 (P0 0.69, port 0.76, SI 0.75). So '+0.25-0.45 given a trigger' is the favourable half of the prior range. Other weak points: (1) Every input is a prior. That includes k, g's sd of 1.0 (the 'second ticket'), rho and the copy rate. Nothing is measured on private data. (2) The submit-time tie order for the port assumes the x138 block ties exactly at full precision. The LB CSV (17:05:53Z) shows only 3 decimals, so this cannot be checked. With a random position inside the tie (early 0.5) the port loses its bronze edge over SI (0.80 vs 0.81 at 150 copies; 0.72 vs 0.78 at 300). (3) The 0.953 block's median SubmissionCount is 25. These are active teams, not one-shot copiers, so the 'copiers keep max(own, Y)' model is optimistic: they will stack their own tweaks on a successor, which lowers every option by ~0.04. (4) The value is conditional on a trigger with P ~10-15%, so the unconditional gain is ~+0.01-0.05 P(bronze). Feasibility: R11S-2 itself is a model, with no code and no submit, so R1-R10 and R8 are not touched. The SI rows are only real if the R11S-4 tooling, tests and HF v3 proxy dummies are committed before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC. Otherwise the table shown to the user must drop the SI rows.
fix: Present the table as INFO (priors, not measurements) with three edits. (a) Replace '+0.25-0.45 bronze swing' with 'about +0.07 to +0.5 given a trigger (low end when the successor's public margin is noise); ~+0.01-0.05 unconditional at P(trigger) 10-15%'. (b) Mark the SI rows 'only if the R11S-4 tooling and proxy dummies land before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC (R8)'. (c) Add one line: the port's early-tie advantage assumes exact full-precision ties, which the 3-decimal LB CSV cannot confirm; with a random tie position, port and SI are equal for bronze and SI stays ahead for silver. Keep 'never drop #37' and 'never {SI, port}'. Do not use the table to justify relaxing any P3/P4b/P4c hygiene clause.
realistic_gain: Given a trigger (a public x138-family successor >= 0.954 that passes the gates), taking any action instead of {#37,#38} gains about +0.07 to +0.5 P(bronze); the central prior is about +0.25-0.3 and the low end comes from the k=0, sd 0.5 case. SI adds about +0.05-0.16 P(silver) over the port. Unconditionally (P(trigger) ~10-15%) this is ~+0.01-0.05 P(bronze) and ~+0.01 P(silver). In the ~85-90% of worlds with no successor it has zero effect, and the model itself has no score effect.
